name: Scalding Mornbrew Delivery
summary: Nori Pridedrift sends you across Coldridge Valley with hot mornbrew for Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar. The mountain cold can steal its heat before it arrives.

sections.title: A Race Against the Frost
sections.body: After you deliver to Grelin Whitebeard, Nori has another cup to send. He cannot carry it himself before the mornbrew freezes into slush. So he asks you to brave the snow and keep his customer from waiting.

sections.title: The Price of a Warm Mug
sections.body: Durnan Furcutter waits inside Anvilmar's warm mountain hall and is particular about his refreshments. He will not take chilled mornbrew. A hot cup gives the weary dwarf a needed break from his duties. Nori expects his favorite mug back in one piece.

faq.answer: Durnan Furcutter is a dwarf in Anvilmar's underground hall in Coldridge Valley. Nori Pridedrift brings him hot mornbrew.

faq.q: Why does the delivery need to be so fast?
faq.answer: The cold in Coldridge Valley cools hot drinks quickly. Durnan ordered scalding mornbrew, and dwarves consider cold ale or tea ruined.
Nori Pridedrift is a dwarf stationed along Coldridge Valley's snowy paths. He carries deliveries between local encampments, including drinks for Grelin Whitebeard and workers in Anvilmar.
Mornbrew is a warm, invigorating dwarven morning brew. It cuts through the chill of the Dun Morogh peaks and sustains hardy mountain workers.
Anvilmar lies northeast of Nori's post, carved into the mountain rock of Coldridge Valley. It shelters young mountaineers and craftsmen from the blizzards.

faq.q: Does Nori want the mug back?
faq.answer: Yes. When Durnan finishes his hot brew, he returns the empty mug for Nori in Coldridge Valley.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you know cold brew in mountain air is a sorrow worth crossing the valley to prevent.
As a cook, you know serving a drink at the proper temperature shows respect, especially in Dun Morogh's bitter cold.
